newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Evans D. sees fair year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INTERVIEW - Evans D. sees fair year.

text.p: Heavy engineering group Evans Deakin Industries Ltd is expecting a reasonable current year's trading while working hard to get the Clyde Industries Ltd subsidiary into shape after a successful takeover.

In an interview with Reuters, Evans Deakin's chairman Ron Paul was confident Clyde was on track to become a successful addition to the EDI stable with full benefits of the takeover coming through in 1997/98.
Rationalising the Sydney-based Clyde operations has been a full-time job for Evans Deakin since gaining control in August after a A$190 million cash-and-share offer in April.

Sticking to its intention to offload what are considered to be non-core assets, EDI has already sold Clyde's 8.16-percent stake in Sunbeam Victa Holdings Ltd to institutions and is still looking for a buyer for Clyde's Ajax Chemicals operation. Paul said that search was still on, as was a review of Clyde's B&D roller door division.
Paul said Clyde, with one of only two licences in Australia to build locomotives, will boost Evans Deakin's chances of hunting down new big contracts both in Australia and overseas.

"We believe that the combination of the two groups will create a major Australian-owned engineering group which will be well positioned to generate new business both in Australia and overseas markets," Paul said.
"The businesses are complementary rather than competitive -- they interlock rather than overlap," he said.
Meanwhile Evans Deakin had won a few major contracts of its own, including the A$100 million-plus light rail contract for Malaysia.
"We have the Kuala Lumpur urban light rail system contract with the first 34 cars completed and already in service for driver training," Paul said.
The remaining 56 carriages would be ready for shipping to Malaysia next month with completion of the whole project awaiting an announcement by the Malaysian Prime Minister, Paul said.

Paul said all the rolling stock had been built at Evan Deakin's Walkers Ltd subsidiary in Maryborough, Queensland. "We've got to keep Australians in work and the skills maintained in our industries," Paul said.

Walkers was also responsible for the design, manufacture and commissioning of Queensland's first high-speed tilt trains scheduled for the Brisbane-Rockampton line late next year. New trains on Queensland Railways high-speed Gold Coast line were also made by Walkers, Paul said.

Evan Deakin's forward order book was currently more than A$270 million including a A$38 million contract for the Boyne Island smelter expansion in Queensland and nearly A$20 million worth of contract for sugar milling equipment in Australia and Vietnam.
